#3567. Want to Smell Bisexual? A Hit Podcast Has the Perfume for You

You Must Remember This is a podcast dedicated, as its host Karina Longworth says in every intro, to exploring the secret and/or forgotten histories of Hollywood’s first century. Longworth, who is an LA–based writer and film preservationist, usually tells her stories in themed seasons. Those include Erotic 90’s, spanning the introduction of the NC-17 rating to Eyes Wide Shut; Dead Blondes (Marilyn Monroe, Jean Harlow, Veronica Lake); and a whole series exploring the web of connections Charles Manson had to Hollywood. It’s addictive, exhaustively researched, and narrated in a way that is both soothing and trancelike.

Longworth is a native Angeleno who has been writing about film for years. She was a film editor and critic at the LA Weekly for three years until 2012; wrote books on Al Pacino and Meryl Streep; and then started You Must Remember This is 2014. She’s also part of a film-loving couple: her husband of 8 years is the Knives Out writer and director Rian Johnson.

The latest season of the podcast is called The Bisexuals, spotlighting the stories of actors and actresses whose love lives were often much more diverse than anything sanctioned by a studio. One star that the season discusses is Libby Holman, a singer and socialite who married the tobacco heir Zachary Smith Reynolds in 1931. Not only did she have a fruitful sex life with Tallulah Bankhead and Montgomery Clift, but she was known for her signature scent called Jungle Gardenia.

In honor of that bombastic perfume that wafted off of her, Longworth, 46, collaborated with Joey Rosin, who formulated a fragrance, Bisexual. Vanity Fair spoke to Longworth about moviegoing in Los Angeles versus New York, what she smelled like as a teenager, being in grad school in your 40s, and her thoughts about Quentin Tarantino’s film programming.

The interview that follows has been condensed for length and clarity.

Vanity Fair: What was the first perfume you remember wearing?

Karina Longworth: Opium by YSL was really a big deal for me when I was 18, 19. It was one of the first perfumes that I ever knew about. I started with The Body Shop’s Tea Rose oil. I didn’t really have any female adult influences because my mom died when I was 11, and so I had to sort of figure out that whole world.

Have you always wanted to make a perfume? Are you a perfume nerd?

So I never had an ambition to make a perfume, but over the past 10 years, I’ve become really into perfume. I used to rent an office space in the same building as an independent perfumer, Jacqueline Ella Steele, whose brand was called Goest— which doesn’t exist anymore—but she made a perfume called Silent Films. She was the first person I contacted about trying to formulate this perfume. But she’s out of business. So that’s when I started asking around and I got led to Joey Rosin.

I got the idea because, in reading and writing about Libby Holman, there are all these anecdotes of her walking into a room in a cloud of Jungle Gardenia, to the point where, people who were attracted to her were attracted to it, and people who didn’t like her found it so disgusting. I thought there was something really interesting about that, how the same scent could be either attractive or repellent, depending on how you felt about the person wearing it.

What does a bisexual smell like? In this case jungles and gardenia

Personalities, voices and clothes all depend on who’s doing it.

There’s this really incredible anecdote in Patricia Bosworth’s Montgomery Clift biography about how one of Montgomery Clift’s friends was at a party at Treetops, Libby Holman’s estate, and she was looking for the bathroom, and accidentally walked into her bedroom, and the bed was a tangle of white satin sheets, and there’s a giant bottle of barbiturates on the nightstand and everything just reeked of Jungle Gardenia. She was grossed out, but then she also got the impression this is Libby and Monty’s sex lair.

We didn’t try to copy the exact old fragrance. Joey does his research, and he did research into what the original notes were. But we talked about not wanting it to be a slavish copy, and instead just trying to evoke for both of us what jungle would smell like with gardenia, and how that could evoke Libby’s story. And so we played around with adding different types of smoke to it.

I’ve been to Tahiti. I’m trying to think if I’ve ever been to a jungle. We talked a lot about tropical plants and what the dirt would smell like, and the heat. It’s like hot weather almost has a smell. But then pairing that with this kind of old lady scent of gardenia. I went to visit his studio in Brooklyn a few times and he mailed some samples to me in Los Angeles. And by that point, it was like four iterations that were almost exactly the same. So it was just about what was giving me the best vibe.

I was living alone in Rochester, N.Y. in a depressing situation because of the weather and being very alone, having no social life.

But you loved your grad school program, right? I forget the name but I know it’s long.

L. Jeffrey Selznick School of Film Preservation at the George Eastman Museum. I got so much out of the program, but it was grueling, physically, and mentally, and emotionally. It was really difficult to suddenly be living alone in a place where I felt like I had no one I could really talk to.

So you were in an entirely new, but temporary situation.

I started relying on scented candles to improve my mood and to change my mood. If I got home feeling terrible, the fragrance was helpful. I also had nowhere to wear perfume. At first I thought I would just make a candle, and then as I started learning more about fragrance, I learned that candles have to go through a much more rigorous process. And it takes a lot longer. We were not going to be able to get it done in time to have a presale like we have during the podcast season. But in the future, I would like to do a signature scent for You Must Remember This and have it available as a perfume and a candle.

It would be classic, but in a different way. I’m very inspired by the signature scent that they have at the Chateau [Marmont].

There has been a lot of talk about moviegoing being back. How has your tour been?

It has been great. In Savannah they sold 400 tickets to a very obscure, pre-code movie on a Friday night.

People must ask you a lot of podcast questions. What are your tips?

I say I don’t know what form yours is going to take, but mine takes the form of writing an extremely detailed script, and then sitting by myself in a room and reading it into a microphone.

I built a recording studio. I bought a little house in Laurel Canyon at the end of a private road, like at the end of a cul-de-sac, but you feel like you’re in the middle of the forest. I bought it from this woman who had lived there for 15 years and was kind of an all-purpose healer. She basically built a soundproof room with clay on the walls and crystals embedded into the clay, where she would do sound baths with them. When I saw this house, it was just perfect.

Which city has a better movie scene, New York or LA?

New York’s way better than LA, but LA is getting better.

Did someone buy the Vista? I loved that theater.

[Quentin] Tarantino owns the Vista. Because it’s Tarantino, he won’t let them show anything digital. It has to be a film print, and so he’ll show a new movie if there’s a print, like The Odyssey played there, Sinners played there. But when there isn’t a new movie out that is on a print, he programs whatever he wants to see. He also does a lot of like Saturday morning matinees of classical Hollywood cinema that is just his taste, you know. Sometimes it’s my taste, sometimes it’s not. It’s a lot of Jerry Lewis. But one thing I will say for Tarantino is that when he discovers a filmmaker or genre or something from the past, he shows. He’s been showing all these William Beaudine silent films, and I think that’s great because silent film has really fallen out of fashion in LA.

I was leaving to interview you today and someone said, “Oh, I love that podcast,” and was talking about the Manson series. Is that your most popular?

It changes. Increasingly, people are asking about the Polly Platt series.

Do you know what the next series is going to be?

I have two ideas that would involve talking to people or family members of subjects who have passed away, but who could give me access to sort of the family lore. I am in contact with both of those families, but I need to kind of do the legwork, talking to them more and figure out which story makes the most sense. I also sketched out a very long season about the three stars of Rebel Without a Cause. That is something that people have been asking me to do for years. But the thing that stops me from doing it is that we still don’t know exactly what happened to Natalie Wood. But that’s kind of in my back pocket.

The Hunger Games movies are once again back on the big screen, and Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters and crushing at the box office. The book to screen adaptation featured a killer cast, including the legendary Glenn Close as Drusilla Sickle. She and Mckenna Grace's Maysilee Donner had slap off in the prequel film, and had thoughts about which one of them had the better one.

Fans of the Hunger Games franchise (which is streaming with a Hulu subscription) were hyped to see a different side to Panem, especially those who read the Sunrise on the Reaping novel. One memorable moment is when Drusilla and Maysilee got into a slapping match on the train, and during a conversation from ET's Instagram, the two actresses joked about who had the better slap. Close responded with:

The Fatal Attraction actress seems to be tipping her hat to Grace, whose character gave her a big slap after the Capitol escort threw hands first. Maysilee is a character with tons of rage, and seeing her defend herself against Drusilla was the audience's first glimpse into that anger.

Of course, Glenn Close's character doesn't take this lightly. She whips out a riding crop and uses it on Maysilee, resulting in the District 12 tribute having welts all over her arms and face. The Oscar-winning actress spoke about this, mentioning:

Well, I ultimately win because I beat you.

Mckenna Grace is a self-described Hunger Games superfan, who seemed thrilled to be playing Maysilee in Sunrise on the Reaping. During the same clip she spoke about how nervous she was for the slap off with Close, offering:

I also worked it up in my head. I was like 'What if a trip? What if I hit Glenn?' And then I was like 'Wait, what if Glenn is kind of method? What if she actually wants to hit me? But I can't morally slap Glenn Close.'

Talk about pressure. Glenn Close is a celebrated icon of the stage and screen, so one can only imagine how daunting it was for Grace to do this scene. Add in that her iconic co-star is 79 years old, accidentally slapping her for real was the thing of nightmares. Luckily that didn't happen, and the scene went viral before the new Hunger Games prequel was even released.

I loved watching the feud between Maysilee and Drusilla during Sunrise on the Reaping, and wish that we got more of their dynamic. There was a ton of content that was cut from the film to keep it short, so maybe we'll get more of this in deleted scenes. Fingers crossed.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters now as part of the 2026 movie release list. Clearly audiences are still invested in Panem, so we'll have to see if/when the franchise continues to expand.

#3564. Here Are Some Super Useful Control Shortcuts GTA 6 Doesn’t Tell You About

I’ve played over 150 hours of Grand Theft Auto 6. You might think I’ve seen it all, and that I know everything there is to know about the game. Nope! I’m still discovering new mechanics, features, and open-world moments after all this time. This includes some very handy control shortcuts I recently learned about that will make your life in Vice City a little easier.

First off, let’s start with the whole reason I wanted to write this blog. Did you know that you can quickly toggle your car radio on and off without having to enter a submenu? All you have to do is double-tap left on the D-pad, and Jason or Lucia will turn the radio on or off.

I had no idea you could do this until I saw people sharing it on Reddit. The game doesn’t explain this shortcut, as far as I can tell. I couldn’t even find it mentioned in the in-game help menu, which does include lots of other nifty tips and tricks.

Here’s another trick I just learned about: You can double-tap the circle/B button while in a car to cycle the headlights between off, high beams, and low beams.

I thought you had to hold left on the D-pad to open up the vehicle submenu to turn off the headlights, but nope! And again, this isn’t mentioned in the help menu and if a prompt appeared during the normal course of the game to explain this, I and many others must have missed it.

Here’s another useful thing you can do inside cars: If you double-tap the triangle/Y button while driving, you’ll exit the vehicle without turning off the engine or radio.

GTA 6‘s help menu does call this out and mentions you can do this at speed to have your car drive into something while you roll out the side to safely. But again, I can’t remember a single time when the game forced me to do this or taught me that it was possible. I learned from a random post online. I guess I should have dug through the help menu more, but come on, who is doing that in Grand Theft Auto?

Another feature mentioned in the help menu that I just learned about is the ability to click the right stick in and yell at nearby drivers. Rockstar refers to this as the road rage button, and it’s a good thing to have in a game where NPC drivers, inspired by real Floridian drivers, suck shit and drive like maniacs.

One more useful control trick: You can double-tap the triangle/Y button while driving a boat to get up and walk around the deck while the boat keeps on cruising.

The next time I boot up GTA 6, I’m going to start double-tapping random buttons during different parts of the game to see what other hidden shortcuts and control options Rockstar has buried in this massive game. And if you want some more useful hidden features, check out this blog about how to flip cars and sit anywhere you want in GTA 6.Â

All the endings (and a couple variations) for GTA 6 we've seen so far.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Obviously, massive spoilers follow for GTA 6 endings!

There are multiple endings to GTA 6, and while we haven't experienced them all personally here at PC Gamer, the gaming community has been sharing them around for anyone curious about what they may have missed.

The ending you get depends on the choices you make during the final GTA 6 story mission, but also depends on how you handled Jason and Lucia's romance and criminal profiles throughout the game, so seeing every version of the ending would mean not just playing the ending multiple times, but having different playthroughs of the game altogether.

There are a couple of endings that I don't consider "different" from each other but do have some differences leading up to them, which I'll explain below. There may also be additional endings we haven't seen yet, so we may update this guide in the future.

In the bridge endings, Jason and Lucia have defeated Mendez and his squad and gotten the hard drive back from Georgio's penthouse and escaped. They drive to Cal's place in Key Lento, but discover he has been compromised. They drive to the bridge, but the cops have set up a roadblock and have the couple trapped. Lucia wants to keep going, but Jason suggests they jump off the bridge and swim for it.

A choice comes up on the screen: "Swim For it" or "No Surrender."

Jason and Lucia try to run the roadblock and are shot to death by cops on the bridge. They die holding hands. In the credits, we see that their son Tomas lives happily with Lucia's aunt, her husband, and their children.

Jason and Lucia are shot to death by cops on the bridge. They die holding hands. In the credits, their lawyer, Abe, brings the money to Lucia's aunt. Tomas lives happily with Lucia's aunt, her husband, and their children in a much bigger house than the other No Surrender ending.

Choosing "Swim for it" presents an additional choice. When Jason gets out of the car, Lucia can choose to "Exit" the car with him, or change her mind by not choosing it.

Jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim for it. They both exit the car without holding guns. Lucia jumps, but Jason doesn't jump and is arrested. Lucia signs a deal for immunity while Jason goes to prison. Lucia gets a job in a diner. Lucia takes Tomas to meet Jason in prison, but he can only see his son through a glass divider.

Jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim for it. Jason exits the car with a gun, but Lucia changes her mind and stays in the car. The police open fire and Jason and Lucia are both shot to death. Tomas lives with Lucia's aunt, her husband, and their children.

Jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim for it, Jason doesn't jump and is arrested. Two years later, Lucia uses the savings account to get Jason freed from prison. Lucia goes to the prison to pick up Jason. Jason meets Tomas and holds his hand.

If you don't have a strong relationship between Jason and Lucia, there is a different ending location: the base of Georgio's tower. In these endings, the couple never makes it to the bridge. You can also choose to break up the couple, either as Jason or as Lucia, as you begin the mission Protective Custody.

After the tower fight with Georgio's men, police confront the couple at the base of the tower. The police open fire and Jason pushes Lucia down. Jason is shot. Lucia has a choice to "Stay down" or "Defend Jason". She stays down and watches Jason die. Lucia is arrested, signs a deal, and visits Tomas at her aunt's house. Lucia then leaves Tomas with her aunt, takes out a gun, and continues her life of crime by preparing to rob a diner.

After the tower fight with Georgio's men, police confront them at the base of the tower. The police open fire and Jason pushes Lucia down. Jason is shot. Lucia chooses "Defend Jason" and fights the cops. They die together.

On the way down to ground level at the tower, Jason decides to run. Lucia is arrested and signs the deal, then lives with her aunt and Tomas while working in a diner. One night there's a knock on the door and she finds a bag of cash on the porch. We see Jason driving away with... Rocco the drug-sniffing dog from earlier in the game. Sure, that might as well happen.

How to get this ending (sourced by GamingwithTZ on YouTube):

Jason and Lucia make a deal with Mendez after defeating him. Once they have the hard drive, they're surrounded by cops at the bottom of the tower. Mendez arrives and takes them away in his car, then drives them to the swamp. Later in the credits, we see two skulls in the swamp, side-by-side, with a bullet hole in each.

Note: You may need a specific criminal profile for this ending. I tried to take the deal (as Lucia) in one of my ending playthroughs, but Jason shot Mendez anyway. I had both Jason and Lucia at "Professional" level criminal profiles. This ending was not available to me. Speculation, but this ending may only be available if you don't have "Professional" as your criminal profiles.

There are potentially (and almost certainly) more endings to GTA 6. There are still a few combinations of all the different variables, including your romance level, criminal profile level, amount of money saved, and the choices you make during the final mission, that we haven't seen yet.

We'll update this guide if the community finds more endings.

#3562. The Surprising History of the Royal Walkabout

“I have to be seen to be believed,” the late Queen Elizabeth II once said. And on Christmas Day, the royal family will be seen en masse during their annual walkabout on their way to services at St. Mary Magdalene Church on the Sandringham estate. For years, the holiday stroll, which features major and minor royals mingling with the public, has been a milestone event on the royal calendar.

But three controversial royals, the former Prince Andrew, Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, almost certainly will not be there. While Andrew has disappeared into his new life at Marsh Farm in Norfolk, Harry and Meghan have continued the tradition of the walkabout, reportedly infuriating the palace with a planned meet-and-greet with a small group of well-wishers in Nottingham. Although no longer working members of the royal family, it seems the couple knows the value and the power of this famous tradition, whose origins are far more recent than many believe.

For centuries, commoners were lucky to get a glimpse of royals riding a horse on a march across the country or nodding from a carriage on the way to the opening of parliament. The first Buckingham Palace balcony appearance was not until 1851, when Prince Albert came upon the idea of Queen Victoria appearing to celebrate the Great Exhibition of London.

The leading figure behind the idea of making the monarchy more visible to the public was a surprising one: the dour, but savvy George V, who ascended the throne in 1910. “I may be uninspiring,” he admitted, “but I’m damned if I’m an alien.”

Queen Elizabeth II and Prince William waving from the balcony of Buckingham Palace during Trooping the Colour on June 16, 1990. Pictured: Prince Edward, Duchess Of York, Queen Mother, Princess Margaret, Queen Elizabeth II, Prince Philip, Prince William, The Grand Duchess Josephine Charlotte Of Luxembourg, Prince Harry, Prince Charles, Lord Frederick Windsor, Princess Diana and Lady Rose Windsor.

These royal appearances ramped up significantly during the first World War, when the royal family came under scrutiny for their German lineage. George visited everyday soldiers on the Front, and Queen Mary and her children spent hours visiting the wounded in hospitals.

“George took ‘getting out and about’ to new levels. He visited industrial areas and poor housing, went down a coal mine and went on a relentless round of opening hospitals and inspecting regiments,” royal news website Royal Central notes. “Queen Mary once retorted to a princess complaining about yet another hospital visit: ‘We are the royal family—and we love hospitals.’”

However, these events were still carefully curated, with a distance maintained between the royal family and those they were visiting. It was not until 1939, that the first unofficial walkabout occurred, when King George VI and Queen Elizabeth (better known as the Queen Mother) went to tour Canada on a goodwill tour in the midst of the looming war. In May, the couple laid a wreath at Ottawa National War Memorial while an estimated 10,000 veterans looked on.

Overcome with emotion, the royal couple decided to go into the crowd to speak with onlookers. A CBC radio journalist watching the scene could hardly have sounded more in awe. “They all look most happy, most excited,” the reporter said. “One had the hand of the queen in one hand and the hand of the king in another. A delighted expression.”

George and Elizabeth were equally touched, and continued these meet-and-greets throughout the tour. “I lost my heart to Canada and to Canadians, and my feelings have not changed with the passage of time,” the Queen Mother recalled.

Known for her effusive personality and warmth, the Queen Mother became a pro at speaking with everyday subjects. During World War II, George and Elizabeth were praised for going among the people in bombed out areas devastated by the Blitz, listening to their woes and offering encouragement and strength.

Queen Elizabeth II on walkabout in Launceston, Tasmania, during her tour of Australia, 1970.

But it was not until Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip toured Australia and New Zealand in 1970 that the modern walkabout was truly introduced into the British royal calendar. There are different origin stories about how the modern walkabout came to be. One version asserts that it was a spontaneous decision of the Queen to walk to her next stop in order to chat, shake hands and accept flowers from schoolchildren in New Zealand.

Others say that first walk was the brainchild of the modernizing Australian courtier William Heseltine, known as the “mastermind behind the monarchy.” A firm believer in making the family seem more approachable and normal, he was also behind the 1969 Royal Family documentary. But if that project proved to be controversial, the walkabout (a term coined as a result of the tour) was a smash hit.

According to Kitty Kelley, the first royal walkabout did not occur in London until 1972, during the celebration of Elizabeth and Philip’s 25th wedding anniversary. “People were agog; their sovereign had never been known to speak to ordinary people,” Kelley writes in The Royals. “This was the first royal walkabout London had ever seen, and flag-waving Britons cheered as the Queen, the Duke of Edinburgh, Prince Charles, and Princess Anne melted into the crowd, greeting people and trying to make the royal family appear less remote.”

While the Queen reportedly enjoyed the intimacy of the walkabout, not every royal family member was quite as thrilled. “At nineteen years old suddenly being dropped in the middle of the street, suddenly being told to pick someone and talk to them,” Princess Anne said. “Fun? No, I don’t think so. A challenge.”

Queen Elizabeth II visits the Town Hall in Sydney with Emmet McDermott, Lord Mayor of Sydney, during her tour of Australia, May 1970.

Soon, the walkabout was a major part of every royal’s schedule, and family members had to learn how to do them—like it or not. “I learnt the way a monkey learns—by watching its parents,” King Charles once said.

During international tours, the walkabouts made a packed schedule even more tiring, but Queen Elizabeth II never faltered. “On a tour of Canada, visiting Saskatchewan, the Canadian minister Alvin Hamilton was concerned that the Queen had been on her feet all day and had not even requested a ‘health break,’” Karen Dolby writes in The Wicked Wit of Queen Elizabeth II. “Her private secretary breezily replied that the Minister for Northern Affairs and National Resources need not worry, ‘Her Majesty is trained for eight hours.’ It’s impossible not to wonder about the training sessions.”

She also leaned upon her sense of humor when meeting folks of all different stripes. “On a walkabout in Scotland, a helpful observer commented that she looked just like the Queen, to which she quickly replied, ‘How reassuring,’” Dolby notes.

According to Dolby, the Queen also developed a system to communicate with her staff while talking with the public. If things were going well, she held her handbag in the crook of her left arm. If she wanted someone to relieve her so she could move on, the handbag was dropped to her side.

But the person who truly transformed the modern walkabout was Princess Diana, much to her husband Prince Charles’s chagrin. “Charles was smart enough to see what a stunning political asset Diana had become—but he was also deeply disturbed by all the adoration coming his young wife’s way,” Tina Brown writes in The Diana Chronicles.

From the start it was clear the young Princess had a connection with everyday people unlike any other royal. During a walkabout while touring Wales in 1981, Charles joked, “I seem to do nothing but collect flowers these days, I know my role.”

As Dianamania swept the world, the Princess became more and more comfortable with connecting with her often-rabid fans. Far from a stiff gloved handshake, she would clasp hands gloveless, hug well-wishers, kneel to speak with children. Frustrated that Diana constantly pulled focus, Charles delivered pithy one-liners with a forced smile. At one walkabout, the crowd openly groaned when they realized Charles was coming to their side, not Diana. “It’s not fair is it?” Charles quipped to the crowd. “You’d better ask for your money back.”

But despite Charles’s jealousy, he could not deny the impact Diana had during these walkabouts. “Everyone was really buoyed up to see her and she was making an effort to go along and speak to people and people appreciated the effort she put into meeting them,” one person she spoke with remembered. “I know it was her job but she gave that little bit extra to people that made her different and stand out.”

“She made people happy,” he noted. “It’s a rare gift.”

Catherine, Princess of Wales, has followed in her mother-in-law’s footsteps as a walkabout all-star. According to historian Robert Jobson, Catherine was initially scared during the walkabout, offering up the stiff refrain, “Thank you so much. We are so delighted to be here,” over and over. But she quickly acclimated and has become known for her chatty and warm ways. “There’s a real art to walkabouts,” she has said. “Everybody teases me in the family that I spend far too long chatting. I still have to learn a little bit more, and to pick up a few more tips, I suppose.”

In fact, it has become a sport for the press to catch Prince William subtly attempting to move Catherine along, often eventually giving up. During the Christmas Day walkabout in 2024, she was the last royal to leave the receiving line, quipping “I think I’ve lost my family!”

According to royal author Robert Hardman, King Charles can also be unusually chatty. No one quite wants to go up and go, ‘Sir, can you get a move on?’ he says. “Instead, Queen Camilla will nudge him in the small of his back with the corner of her handbag.”

But the predilection is one Camilla shares as well. On a walkabout in Wrexham, an irritated Charles was overheard telling an aide “Can we try to get [Camilla] back again? Please? We need to go! I was trying to wait for her, but she goes on!”

Prince Harry and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, attend University of the South Pacific on October 24, 2018 in Suva, Fiji.

Learning the art of the walkabout—what to say, what not to say—is a lesson every royal must figure out, often on the job. When Meghan Markle married Prince Harry in 2018, she admitted her ignorance. “I never saw pictures or videos of a walkabout,” she claimed.

And with the advent of cell phones, the job has become much more difficult. “I’m glad that I’m not starting now because at least you had people to talk to. Now you don’t really. Phones are bad enough, but the iPads—you can’t even see their heads,” Princess Anne said.

And these engagements can occasionally go south. In 2018, the Duchess of Sussex was rushed out of a market in Fiji after the walkabout got out of hand. There are also the occasional overzealous fans, including recently when a woman attempted to kiss Prince William on the cheek. And who can forget the supremely uncomfortable walkabout at Windsor after the Queen’s death in 2022, when a warring William, Catherine, Harry and Meghan greeted public mourners. It was, Catherine reportedly said, “one of the hardest things she’d ever had to do.”

Walkabouts are also a logistical headache for royal protection officers. “You are always aware of who is in the crowd,” former royal bodyguard Simon Morgan explained to Hello! “That is one of the positives of our royal family, they always want to go and meet people and as a protection officer, you have to accept what their wishes are. The current trend of hugs, high fives and selfies, that’s going to continue, so the protection officer’s job is really brought to the front then, because the protection officer is constantly looking for what could go wrong, you are constantly working things through your mind for the ‘what if, what if, what if.’

But the walkabout shows no sign of disappearing anytime soon. And come Christmas Day, there will be cheers, hugs, and an enormous amount of quick, polite chats about the weather that citizens who wait and brave the winter cold will never forget.

That betrayal inspired an entire fandom of Dragon Age players who either wanted to redeem him when he returned as the big bad in Veilguard or, like I and many others wanted, to kill him. â Ash Parrish

His romance asks players to consider that very real part of life in a way that just doesnât get depicted in video games. AND!!! The fact that Emmrich is an old man doesnât mean the sex is dry and boring. I was delightedâdelighted I tell you!âwhen in the postcoital afterglow he was up, walking around and asking my Rook if she wanted some food while I was still half in bed. Old man broke MY back. Respect. â Ash Parrish

Alistair is the number one BioWare cutie patootie. In Dragon Age: Origins heâs just a good wholesome farm boy conscripted into drinking demon blood that will eventually kill him. Alistair was my very first BioWare romance and I instantly fell for his golden-retriever charm. Despite his sad orphan upbringing and his doomed existence as a Grey Warden, Alistair never loses his goofy charm. The Iron Bull is to Dragon Age romances what Garrus and Tali are to Mass Effect romances in that I canât believeâbut am delightedâthat BioWare went for it and made the most ânon-humanâ character in your squad actually romanceable. Morrigan from Dragon Age: Origins, with her dark makeup and impossible outfit literally held together with string, seems like an âI can fix herâ romance when actually sheâs a âShe can make me worseâ girl. Sis is a meme in the Dragon Age community mocking how anything the Grey Warden does that could even remotely be construed as heroic is met with the iconic pop-up, âMorrigan disapproves.âÂ

She is the mean girl to end all mean girls, and that doesnât go away when you romance her. Her fierce dedication to her independence no matter her relationship status makes her one of those rare companions that makes you feel like youâve fallen for a real person. A male Grey Warden can conceive a child with her, one you see grow throughout the Dragon Age quadrilogy, but except for a few brief moments throughout the series, the Grey Warden never really gets the chance to settle down with his family, making her romance part love story, part tragedy. â Ash Parrish

Kaidan is the first male love interest in the Mass Effect series, but in truth, his romantic relationship is best when viewed as a slow burn across the entire trilogy. Thatâs why a romantic relationship with him as Male Shepard, which was only made an option in Mass Effect 3 when BioWare decided to finally implement same-sex relationships for men, is one of the most profound love stories in the series. It suggests Kaidan and Shepard have been pining for each other for years, only to finally confess their feelings as the entire world is ending around them. Every kiss stolen between missions and military meetings is making up for years of âwill-they-wonât-theysâ and all that time they spent not even speaking to each other during Mass Effect 2. Now, theyâre finally considering a future with one another that they donât even know if theyâll get to have. The galaxy rests on their shoulders, but their sights are set on something smaller: the chance to spend just one more second of time together after all the time they foolishly wasted getting to this point. This all culminates in the twoâs first and only on-screen âI love youâ as Shepard makes a dash for the Citadel at the end of Mass Effect 3, hoping that whatever he finds there might guarantee that future, or, if it canât, at least create one that Kaidan is alive to see. â Kenneth Shepard

As a Mass Effect diehard, I have a soft spot for KOTORâs Carth because heâs voiced by Kaidan actor Raphael Sbarge, but I will also give his romance, in which he reckons with the loss of one life and tries to imagine another, its flowers as one of BioWareâs early examples of a relationship tinged with grief and loss. He had a family once, and he lost them in an orbital strike by the Republic; his desire for revenge consumed him. Like many good revenge stories, KOTOR sees its would-be avenger reckon with what comes after the deed has been done, and if youâre pursuing a relationship with him, it might be you. BioWare games have you meet people at various stages of their lives, and thereâs something poignant about knowing that you might not have been your partnerâs first love, and that theyâve lived lives full of both triumph and tragedy. Carth canât change the past, but youâre there to help him envision something new waiting for him on the other side of this struggle. â Kenneth Shepard

The Fenris romance is like a recipe that calls for you to add a little bit of spice, but you accidentally pour the entire bottle of hot sauce into the concoction and then realize thatâs exactly what it needed. Fenris is an angry person, having been forced into slavery under the Tevinter magisters and conditioned to view magic with skepticism at best, disdain at worst. So, what if he fell in love with a mage that he could not have been more ideologically opposed to? The Rivalry Romance, in which Dragon Age II protagonist Hawke repeatedly calls him out on his absolute hatred of magic users,hits with the kind of intensity your favorite AO3 fanfic can only dream of. Itâs hot, heavy, heart-wrenching and, if you commit to doing the work to trust one another, has a happy ending.Â  Well, as happy as Dragon Age II can muster, I suppose. Trust in the face of a lifetime of conditioning is hard to come by, and allowing yourself to be vulnerable to something youâve been taught doesnât see you as a person feels downright impossible. Yet Fenris and Hawke find a way. â Kenneth Shepard

Despite the fantastical framing, Dorianâs love story in Dragon Age: Inquisition is one that too many queer people are familiar with. He comes from an unsupportive family, having fled his home in Tevinter after his sexuality interfered with their planned legacy. Despite Dorianâs self-assured nature, entering a relationship with him can sometimes feel like stepping into a minefield filled with past traumas, only for them to blow up in your face. But what keeps the relationship afloat is his desire to unpack all the damage thatâs been done with the Inquisitor by his side, and build something better in the space thatâs left. Every queer person has some level of trauma to overcome, and even if he, like most of us, canât deal with his trauma perfectly, his desire to do the work, and do it with someone, is why Dorianâs relationship works, even though heâs been given every reason to believe it canât. â Kenneth Shepard

#3560. Rep. Jimmy Gomez Resigns After Alleged 'Unwanted Sexual Contact' With Aide

Democratic Rep. Jimmy Gomez is resigning from Congress after a House Ethics Committee report determined he allegedly made “unwanted sexual advances” and “sexual contact” with a congressional aide.

“I have strong disagreements with the committee’s report and its conclusions. Among other significant deficiencies and omissions, the report does not include key portions of my testimony that are essential to a full and fair understanding of what occurred,” Gomez, 51, said in a statement to CNN on Monday, November 23. “I also have serious concerns about the process. In my interview, I answered the Committee’s questions only to see my statements selectively quoted, disparaged and disregarded throughout the final report, to which I was given no opportunity to respond.”

The California politician added, “With this in mind, I see no other alternative than to resign, effective December 1, to allow for my staff to close out important constituent casework and needs.”

Us has reached out to Gomez’s team for comment regarding the report and his resignation.

The ethics panel made the Gomez report public on Monday. According to CNN, the report found that Gomez — who lost his bid for re-election this year after serving more than nine years in congress— “failed in his obligation to behave in a manner that reflects creditably on the House, and his conduct was exacerbated by his failure to appreciate the inherent power imbalance between House Members and House staff.”

In its report, the committee also called for “zero tolerance of unwanted sexual advances toward House staff.”

MS Now also reported that a woman, identified only as Witness 1 in the report, alleged to the committee that she had more than one physical encounter with Gomez and did not consider them to be consensual.

She described two incidents, which allegedly occurred in 2024, to the committee, claiming the incident was “nonconsensual whatsoever” and said she remembered “feeling very uncomfortable” and “mortified.”

Attorneys representing the woman praised the committee for its “thorough and sensitive” handling of the investigation.

In January 2023, Gomez — who represented California’s 34th Congressional District — went viral when he appeared in Washington, D.C., to cast his vote for House Speaker with his then 4-month-old son, Hodge.

“In the end, we have to normalize dads taking their kids with them, be it stay-at-home dads or working dads,” Gomez told Today.com at the time. “When I took him to the floor, I think people were surprised — but it wasn’t a big deal. I think it does send a powerful message that us guys need to do our part. We don’t risk our lives bringing children into the world — women do.”

If you or someone you know has been sexually assaulted, contact the National Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-656-HOPE (4673).

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I have watched enough seasons of Survivor to understand the game and have opinions, but not enough to drop Survivor lore. Therefore, I care about the show. It just doesn’t have some of the same dedication and loyalty from me as other reality TV shows. This may be why 2-hour episodes seem like another one of Survivor’s problems.

The last thing Survivor needs is 2-hour episodes.

From years of watching Big Brother, which you can also do with my Paramount+ subscription, I have seen what happens when a reality TV show has far more time than it needs: it misuses it. I don’t want to endure that with Survivor. It doesn’t need an extra 30 minutes. Nothing good can come out of that. We will likely get more fluff and filler, and things that don’t move the story along. More time doesn’t mean a show will effectively use it. We won’t get a season’s maximum potential with more time.

Additionally, Big Brother and similar shows aren’t the only ones to waste the extra time. Netflix reality TV shows play fast and loose with the runtimes. Sometimes the Netflix reality TV shows benefit from a few extra minutes. Other times it feels excessive and boring. I haven't been convinced any reality TV show needs two-hour episodes.

Survivor has worked out earlier issues with the 90-minute format; it doesn’t need to figure out 2 hours.

In the last few seasons, Survivor made some infuriating, questionable choices, so I don’t trust the show to make the best decisions with 2-hour episodes.

When Paramount+ announced a plan to lean more into reality TV, I expected more reality TV. They have announced a few new shows, but not nearly as many or as promising as expected. They have five TV shows under the Paramount+ banner that they could capitalize on with spin-offs. I will always scream to bring Big Brother: Over the Top and Big Brother: Reindeer Games back, but I am open to other ideas to expand that franchise, along with Survivor, The Amazing Race, The Challenge, and RuPaul’s Drag Race.

Instead of giving Survivor 2 hours, pair it with a new Survivor spin-off show to retain some of those viewers. Additionally, I actually prefer watching Survivor with The Amazing Race or another staple CBS reality TV show. I don’t just want a night of only Survivor. Now could be the perfect time to test out a shorter season of Big Brother with Survivor. Create a mini-Big Brother: All Stars spin-off series that only lasts for 30 days, similar to Survivor's length. This could bring in more viewers for each show.

I will gladly watch a three-hour movie (not gladly, but I will do it), but a TV show is pushing it with 2-hour episodes. If Survivor starts doing that, what’s to stop Big Brother, The Amazing Race, and some other reality TV shows?

I personally would be living a nightmare. We have to start limiting how many contestant packages we must see per episode. Change can be good, but this feels like another unnecessary update to the game and viewing.

Spent most of my life in various parts of Illinois, including attending college in Evanston. I have been a life long lover of pop culture, especially television, turned that passion into writing about all things entertainment related. When I'm not writing about pop culture, I can be found channeling Gordon Ramsay by kicking people out the kitchen.

Deborah Ann Woll said she felt "totally unbothered" by the small but vocal subset of gamers who were upset by the upcoming God of War: Laufey, and apparently she meant it—because today Amazon MGM Studios announced that she's going to play the same role in the live-action God of War series coming to Prime.

Just as in God of War: Laufey and its predecessor, God of War: Ragnarok, Woll—best known for playing Karen Page in Marvel's Daredevil, Defenders, and Punisher TV series, as well as a lengthy stint on True Blood as Jessica Hamby—will portray Faye, wife of Kratos and mother of Atreus.

"Faye’s abrupt passing sets in motion the events of God of War," the announcement says. "Along their journey, Kratos and Atreus discover secrets about Faye that make them wonder how well they truly knew her at all."

It's been a bumpy road for the God of War series. It was first reported in 2022, but started over from scratch two years later after the showrunner and executive producers quit. We got our first look at Ryan Hurst as Kratos earlier this year—not very impressive, but we all had the same initial impression of Henry Cavill as Geralt and that worked out well—but then Hurst had to be recast because of an on-set injury; Dave Bautista now has the lead role. Child actors Callum Vinson and Island Austin, who played Atreus and Thrud, were also recast.

God of War: Laufey is set to launch on May 20, 2027, but sadly is a PlayStation 5 exclusive, a state of affairs that seems likely to endure given Sony's recent strategy shift. The God of War live action series on Prime has been ordered for two seasons, but a release target hasn't been announced.

#3557. Red Dead Redemption Movie And TV Rights Could Reportedly Cost $100 Million

Grand Theft Auto VIGTA 6MoviesRed Dead Redemption 2Rockstar Games

With many legacy franchises in decline and few new ones taking off, Hollywood has turned to video games for big box office blockbusters. There have been huge success stories like Minecraft and big bombs like Borderlands. But some of the biggest video game series have yet to make the jump to the silvers screen. Chief among them is Grand Theft Auto. Could that be about to change?

According to a report in The Ankler this week, the answer is no. Multiple sources told the outlet that Rockstar Games isn’t interested in doing a movie adaptation of GTA. It makes sense, in a way, since GTA has increasingly become a series about bringing prestige, cinematic storytelling to the messy, systems-driven gameplay of open-world gaming. Putting that engine in reverse would be a bit like turning the video game version of Indiana Jones back into a movie. Who would ever do that?

But it sounds like Rockstar, owned by Take-Two, is interested in shopping around the rights for a movie or TV adaptation of its Western open-world series, Red Dead Redemption. The Ankler adds that a number of $100 million was at one point thrown around for the price of licensing Red Dead. It points out that Amazon paid $250 million for the TV rights to Lord of the Rings.

Red Dead is in a similar lane to The Last of Us, which HBO managed to thread the needle on making into a prestige television show that still hooked fans of the game. It’s easy to imagine a similarly placed streamer doing the same for Rockstar’s IP, with internal executives pointing to mood boards that include the critical success of things like Deadwood and the commercial appeal of things like Yellowstone.

âWeâre very careful about line extensions because this is a creative company and our goal is to make the best entertainment on earth. Entertainment weâre always proud of,â Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, who used to be COO at 20th Century Fox, said in an interview on The David Rubenstein Show November 12. âWe would make a movie or television show based on our intellectual property if our creative teams were passionate about it. If they thought that would somehow engage and delight our consumers. Itâs a high bar to do that. And of course, thereâs always a risk of failure. So we donât rule it out, but weâre very, very selective.â

He’d given shareholders a more detailed account of this reasoning back in 2023 during Hollywood’s Barbenheimer-craze”

The hit ratios in the motion picture business are vastly lower than they are in the interactive entertainment business. Our hit ratios for console properties are in the 80 percent or 90 percent. The hit ratio for a well-run movie studio is around 30 percent, which is to say there’s a 70 percent chance that the movie that we license could fail. And so in success, the number, in terms of the benefit to our bottom line…it’s not zero, but it’s not really material to what we do around here. And in failure, we run the risk of compromising the underlying intellectual property.

The race to adapt other popular game franchises is already well underway. According to The Ankler, Amazon, Netflix, and FX are paying between $15 million and $25 million per episode for adaptations of Tomb Raider, Assassin’s Creed, and Far Cry. Those are essentially mid-range Hollywood blockbuster budgets.

But Take-Two hasn’t rushed to turn its IP into streaming adaptations, and following the disaster that was the Borderlands movie, which was in production prior to it acquiring series maker Gearbox Entertainment, it has good reason to be. It’s games are already breaking sales and revenue records that Hollywood can’t compete with (GTA 6‘s day-one revenue eclipsed Avengers: Endgame). Why jeopardize that for a small side deal? A good Red Dead show could help the game sell ten million more copies, but a bad one could severely hamper its growing popularity beyond traditional gaming audiences.

“They thought weâd be blinded by the lights and that just wasn’t the case,” Rockstar cofounder Dan Houser, who left to form his own entertainment company, said last year when talking about past discussions. “We had what we considered to be multi billion dollar IP, and the economics never made sense. The risk never made sense. In those days, the perception was that games made poor-quality movies.”

A 2008 adaptation of Max Payne, which Remedy Entertainment developed but Rockstar publishes, starred Mark Wahlberg and was moderately successful at the box office but critically panned with a 15 percent on Rotten Tomatoes. The misstep didn’t doom the series, which eventually got Max Payne 3 and is currently slated for remakes of the first two games, but it’s clearly not the sort of thing Rockstar or Take-Two are interested in repeating, especially when legacy movie studios are in the decline and they’re the entertainment industry’s new big shots.

#3556. Kate Middleton Wore Matching Amethyst Necklace and Earrings for Her First Engagement in India

The Princess of Wales touched down in India this Monday for a whirlwind three-day visit to the country with her husband, Prince William.

The couple visited Mumbai for the sixth Earthshot Prize Summit, which took place on Tuesday. It marked the Waleses’ first joint overseas visit since Catherine’s cancer diagnosis.

The busy schedule of engagements kicked off with a game of gully cricket—an informal version of the game played on the street. For the occasion, the Princess of Wales struck a balance between polished and casual, opting for crisp white Alexander McQueen trousers, paired with a white top layered under a pistachio blazer by Veronica Beard.

The Princess of Wales debuted a pistachio blazer by Veronica Beard for the outing

The finishing touch? A matching set of green amethyst earrings and a drop necklace from one of Catherine’s favorite jewelry labels, Kiki McDonough. Catherine has at least 20 pairs of earrings from the jeweler, ranging from the blue topaz drops she wore to Royal Ascot to the green tourmaline, green amethyst and diamond earrings set in gold, designed specially for her to mark Princess Charlotte’s birth.

The apple green amethysts, which she wore in Mumbai, are among the lesser-seen designs in her collection but proved the perfect accessory for this first engagement.

While in Mumbai, the prince’s program focused on The Earthshot Prize and its mission to accelerate solutions to the world’s most pressing environmental challenges. The princess joined the prince for a number of engagements during the visit.

The Prince and Princess of Wales in Mumbai on Monday

During their time in Mumbai, the prince and princess also celebrated several of the deep cultural connections between the United Kingdom and India: cricket, fashion, and cinema.

Beginning with an engagement focused on the uniquely Indian passion of gully cricket andconcluding with a visit to the heart of Mumbai’s film industry, their royal highnessescelebrated the creativity, talent, and cultural influence that continue to shape modern India andstrengthen ties between the two countries.

The highlight of the visit was the Earthshot Prize ceremony on Tuesday, November 17. Five Earthshot leaders were given 1 million euros (about $1.1 million USD) to accelerate the impact of their innovative solutions. Mumbai made perfect sense as the host city; India is home to more Earthshot Prize winners and finalists than any other country.

The Princess of Wales looked elegant in a lime green blazer layered over an all-white ensemble

Since founding the prize in 2020, Prince William has attended all of the awards ceremonies: in London, Boston, Singapore, Cape Town, and Rio de Janeiro. Catherine joined the prince in London in 2021 and again in Boston the following year, but has missed recent editions in the further corners of the globe. This was partly due to the princess’s restricted work schedule while she underwent treatment for cancer and spent time in recovery.

It marked a return to the country for Prince William and Kate, who carried out a state visit in April 2016. The week-long tour saw the then Duke and Duchess of Cambridge explore Mumbai, New Delhi, Assam, and Bhutan, racking up a total of 22 engagements that saw them try their hand at cricket, meet Bollywood stars and royalty, and champion charitable causes close to their hearts.

It was one of four overseas trips taken by the couple that year. Although William and Kate still travel, it is with far less frequency as the couple prioritizes a stable family life. Their last major overseas tour was to the Caribbean in 2022.

#3555. Mom Arrested After Falsely Claiming Daughter, 4, Was Diagnosed With Cancer

An Ohio mother has been accused of knowingly lying about her daughter’s alleged leukemia diagnosis, forcing the child to undergo unnecessary and painful treatments.

Danielle Rowan was arrested on November 13 and charged with endangering the welfare of children.

Authorities became aware of the allegations when officers with the Powell Police Department responded to a home on November 10 after they received reports of a domestic dispute, according to a probable cause arrest affidavit viewed by Law & Crime.

Rowan and her husband got into an argument when the husband demanded to see their daughter’s medical records. The husband then reportedly took the girl and her sister to Rowan’s parents’ house, where the defendant later showed up and allegedly demanded she give her daughter medication.

Rowan, 32, also allegedly claimed she was the only person who could administer the medication.

Rowan’s husband and her parents explained to authorities in a second call to police that Rowan had claimed her daughter had been diagnosed with leukemia in May.

After Rowan announced the diagnosis, the girl allegedly received several steroid injections that caused her to gain weight and become irritable.

The family later grew suspicious of the girl’s diagnosis when further treatment was continuously delayed, including having a semi-permanent IV line installed. After Rowan allegedly showed her family the cancer diagnosis from the Cincinnati Children’s Hospital’s oncology department, her family members showed the document to a doctor who reportedly confirmed the so-called report was fake.

The family then had a doctor at a children’s hospital examine the girl, who determined she did not have cancer.

Rowan has also been accused of falsely telling a pediatrician that her daughter could not eat solid food, which prompted the doctor to prescribe the child high-calorie PediaSure. The defendant allegedly gave her daughter three to four bottles of the PediaSure each day, which caused her to suffer pain and regular constipation.

Rowan eventually spoke to investigators, at which point she allegedly denied telling anyone her daughter had cancer. However, the detective presented her with her social media posts in which she publicly talked about her daughter’s faux diagnosis. Rowan then claimed to authorities that she “did not remember making the posts.”

Rowan was taken into custody at Delaware County Jail following her arrest. She’s since been released after posting bond.

Following Rowan’s arrest, one of her friends admitted to WBNS that she was shocked to learn of the allegations.

“That’s not the Danielle that I knew, but at this rate, what did I know? What didn’t I know? What is true? What’s not true?” the friend said.

It’s not currently clear if Rowan has entered a plea or retained legal counsel following her arrest. The Delaware County Sheriff’s Office did not immediately respond to Us’ request for comment regarding updates in the case.

It's a very exciting time in the MCU, as we're less a month away from the next upcoming Marvel movie, Avengers: Doomsday. The movie is a thrilling concept for fans who spent years watching the Marvel movies in order, as it features entire teams of superheroes uniting against Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom. The first Doomsday trailer was exciting, but the latest (and final) one has bombshell moments from Steve Rogers and Cyclops.

What we know about Avengers: Doomsday is limited, thanks to Marvel's tight security. That's why the new trailer (seen above) is so thrilling, as it offers way more of what we'll get when it arrives in December. To start, we get way more context about Steve and Peggy's happy ending after Endgame. While Avengers Endgame: Encore had Loki showing up during their dance, we'll see as they have years together, raising their son into a full-blown teen. That explains how he gets the long hair and beard that we've been seeing in the footage.

Moviegoers are also psyched about seeing the OG stars of the X-Men movies in the shared universe, and we got more thrilling content from the mutants in this trailer. While we've seen them fighting the Avengers, this trailer showed the two teams uniting against Sentinels. What's more, James Marsden's Cyclops even utters the iconic line:

The shot of the heroes assembling is the thing of nerdy dreams, with the X-Men being teleported into the battlefield courtesy of Alan Cumming's Nightcrawler. Seeing the mutants alongside Steve Rogers, Sam Wilson, Thor, and Reed Richards is downright epic, especially since Cyclops said that beloved line that's been uttered in the comics, as well as X-Men '97 (which is streaming with a Disney+ subscription).

There's plenty of new footage in this trailer, including some epic shots of the movie's action. We also got the first look at Hailee Steinfeld's return as Kate Bishop, which the actress/singer confirmed over the weekend. She's seemingly sharing a scene with Kathryn Newton's Cassie Lang, so maybe the Young Avengers will finally be formed during this movie's mysterious runtime. Of course, fans of Hawkeye mostly want to see Kate and Florence Pugh's Yelena reunite given their A+ chemistry in the MCU series.

While we got plenty of new content in this trailer, there are still countless questions about what The Russo Brothers have up their sleeve for the next Avengers movie. There are tons of characters in play, and just about anything is possible in the Multiverse Saga. Unfortunately, we didn't get any footage of Elizabeth Olsen's Scarlet Witch following her return in VisionQuest, but fans think that she's one of the Latverian Witches that are shown.

Our countless questions will be answered when Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters on December 18th as part of the 2026 movie release list. Since this is seemingly the final trailer, we might not be getting any more footage until its released.

#3553. GTA 6 Makes Fun Of Call Of Duty With A Joke About Unions While Rockstar Devs Are Voting To Unionize

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rockstar GamesUnion

Grand Theft Auto 6 is launching at the same time Rockstar developers are voting on the future of their union. Meanwhile, 31 former employees have been fighting Rockstar in court over claims they were fired as part of union-busting tactics, which the company denies. All of this makes a silly Call of Duty parody commercial in GTA 6 far more interesting, as the ad directly references unionizing and its benefits.

In GTA 6, you can find many radio stations playing hundreds of songs. But these stations also have DJs and commercials, including ads for in-universe movies, books, shows, and even video games. One of these ads is for the new AAA military shooter Righteous Slaughter: Domestic Infection, the latest entry in the GTA universe’s satirical spin on Call of Duty. The ad claims the biggest threat to the country is a disease that makes people think “anti-American thoughts.” One sign someone has been infected with the “Liberal Cuck Contagion”? They start thinking about fair wages and unions.

Towards the end of the ad, two soldiers fighting to stop the disease have this exchange:

Soldier 1: “You know, we’ve been working on this mission with no benefits, no security…”

Soldier 1: “Maybe we should look into… unionizing?”

Soldier 2: “They got Jimmy! I repeat, Jimmy’s infected!!!”

In a vacuum, it’s a funny skewering of how military shooters tend to be more conservative in their politics, often presenting soldiers as heroes of American values and the way these same right-wing folks often hate concepts, like unions, that improve people’s lives.

But in the context of the ongoing union recognition vote and court battle in the UK over Rockstar’s firing of 31 employees who were involved in union activities at the studio, this joke hits differently. It almost feels subversive, like the people who helped write and produce this ad in GTA 6 are punching back at their own bosses and the folks at the very top of Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two Interactive. Currently, both sides are awaiting the judge’s ruling.Â

“With a recognised union, we can ensure everyone, across every department, sees a fair share of the success we contributed to,” wrote Rockstar developer and union member Nestor Uriarte in The Guardian recently. “Our games are industry-leading. Our wages, conditions and bonuses should be too.”

“Whatever happens in this ballot, our union will continue fighting for a studio that works for every single person at Rockstar, and for workers across the industry. Unionising shouldnât be something we simply admire from afar when dockers, miners or teachers do it. Itâs something we can, and must, embrace for ourselves. The future of the industry shouldnât be a game played over our heads.”

Spoiler: It doesn't actually run at 60 fps.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Clever Grand Theft Auto 6 players have found a glitch with the Xbox version of the game that allows players to forcibly remove Rockstar's 30 fps cap. But even though people claim the game jumps up to 60 fps, the actual performance is nowhere near as smooth, according to Digital Foundry's tests.

The glitch is surprisingly simple to perform: You just need to set the console's output to 60 Hz, load GTA 6, swap the output to 120 Hz, load a different game, and then use the Quick Resume feature to go back to GTA 6. For whatever reason, this forces the game to run above 30 fps, but not by much.

In Digital Foundry's testing, GTA 6 doesn't suddenly become a buttery smooth 60 fps dream. Instead, it has an average frame rate of about 36 fps and still drops below that number during particularly intense scenes, like in city areas or when multiple cars are exploding due to rocket launcher hijinks.

The most notable improvement is lower input lag when it manages to climb up to around 40 fps, but even that has an asterisk because the frame rate varies too much for the benefits to be consistent. Unless you plan on spending your time in Leonida roleplaying as a fisherman, you're going to have a bad time.

While Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers said an official 60 fps mode for GTA 6 is too much for the current generation of consoles to handle, including the PS5 Pro, Digital Foundry theorizes that a 40 fps mode might be possible in the future.

I'm hopeful for console players, but none of this has stopped me from wanting the game on the only platform where 60 fps won't be much of a challenge to hit: PC. Tweaking settings you don't care as much about to juice the frame rate is much preferable over having to deal with a set "performance" mode or a glitch that could be patched out any day. A good PC version should be able to nicely scale up or down in performance based on your hardware setup, and Rockstar has shown that it can pull that off in the past with games like Red Dead Redemption 2.

For a game as good as GTA 6—Chris says it's "(mostly) great" in his 100-hour impressions— you shouldn't have to deal with quirks that tarnish the experience. I'm not a Rockstar employee, I don't know what challenges a PC version introduces or why it wasn't prioritized for a simultaneous PC and console release, but I do know that a PC version likely won't have as many caveats when it comes to performance as it does on consoles. So, I'll deal with Rockstar's intended 30 fps cap until the moment I can boot up GTA 6 on my PC, and then forget that I ever had to endure the limits of the current console experience.
